title: Pilot Runtime LTS with 2 enterprise accounts (Dedicated + Private)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Objective
Run a controlled pilot of the new Runtime LTS channel with 2 enterprise accounts to validate: (1) patch cadence + comms, (2) backport request intake + approvals, (3) perf/correctness gates, and (4) packaging + pinning for Dedicated and Private.

Scope
- LTS line: runtime-1.18-lts
- Target patches during pilot: 1.18.1-lts (initial), plus at least one follow-on patch or an out-of-band security hotfix simulation.
- Deployments: 1 Dedicated customer on Redwood-managed dedicated pools; 1 Private customer using installer/Helm pinning.

Pilot owners
- Release execution: Connor O’Brien
- Runtime: Noah Patel (arch), Hiro Tanaka (kernels), Sofia Ivanova (scheduling)
- Perf gates: Marcus Reed
- CI/build + artifacts: Sahana Iyer
- SRE readiness + monitoring: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- CS coordination: Rachel Kim / Liam O’Rourke
- Support intake: Dev Patel / Owen Phillips

Pilot accounts (proposed)
1) Northstar Bank (regulated prospect; Dedicated-first, strong change-control requirements)
2) Helio Health (healthcare; Private evaluation, explicit asks for pinning + checksums/SBOM)

Non-goals
- Proving feature parity with mainline.
- Expanding LTS to broad GA customer set (this ticket is strictly pilot validation).

Exit criteria for pilot completion
- Two successful customer upgrades to 1.18.1-lts with documented validation + rollback plan.
- At least one backport request processed end-to-end (intake → severity/risk scoring → approvals → cherry-pick PR → CI/perf gates → artifact publish → customer comms).
- Perf gate signal validated as “actionable” (no false positives blocking for >24h without an explicit waiver path).
- Private pinning verified: customer can pin to exact image/tag, verify checksums, and roll back to prior LTS patch.
- Support/CS confirm playbook works: required diagnostics, ETA expectations, and patch availability messaging.

Deliverables
- Pilot plan + schedule (dates, owners, comms)
- Customer validation checklist results (perf + correctness + operational)
- Pilot retro with actions for GA (automation gaps, docs gaps, gating threshold adjustments)

References
- Confluence: runtime LTS branch/backport policy; LTS release runbook; perf gate thresholds; Private upgrade/rollback guidance; LTS support playbook
- Linear: ENG-4821 epic
- GitHub: LTS branch and first patch PRs
acceptance_criteria:
- Accounts selected and confirmed with CS + AE, with written expectations on cadence, scope, and how to escalate.
- Dedicated pilot: customer traffic moved to runtime-1.18.1-lts on a dedicated pool with monitoring and rollback tested.
- Private pilot: customer pins runtime image to 1.18.1-lts, verifies checksums/provenance, completes upgrade + rollback drill.
- One end-to-end backport request completed and communicated (including release notes entry and known-issues updates as needed).
- Pilot retro completed with concrete GA action items and owners.
pilot_accounts:
Candidate A (Dedicated): Northstar Bank
- Driver: deal/security review requires stable baseline + predictable patch cadence.
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated GPU pool; requires strong perf stability and explicit rollback.
- Stakeholders: Rachel Kim (CS), Avery Johnson (AE), Sean Gallagher (SRE).

Candidate B (Private): Helio Health
- Driver: Private deployment requires pinning + verifiable artifacts (checksums, provenance; SBOM if available).
- Environment: Private installer + Helm; customer-managed networking; wants upgrade sequencing + rollback.
- Stakeholders: Liam O’Rourke (TAM), Hannah Schmitt (AE), Sahana Iyer (build), Bruno Silva (installer/helm).
plan:
1) Confirm pilot accounts + success criteria
- Get customer confirmation on: support window expectations, cadence, what qualifies for backport, and expected response time for security patches.
- Ensure both customers understand LTS is stability-first (slower-change) and not feature-forward.

2) Prep internal readiness
- Ensure perf-canary gating capacity reserved for patch week; define waiver process owner (Release Eng + SRE).
- Confirm artifact signing/checksums pipeline and where customers retrieve/verifiy.
- Confirm support intake: template required fields, routing, and severity mapping.

3) Patch schedule + rollout
- Cut 1.18.1-lts RC, run CI + perf gates, run release readiness review (SRE).
- Roll Dedicated customer first (lower operational friction): canary → ramp → steady-state.
- Roll Private customer with a prescriptive checklist; do a rollback drill.

4) Backport request drill
- Use a real Sev1/Sev2 fix if it arises during pilot; otherwise run a “tabletop” backport request using a known candidate fix to validate process and comms.

5) Report + retro
- Collect metrics: perf deltas, incidents, support tickets, time-to-backport, and customer qualitative feedback.
- Write pilot retro + GA recommendations; update runbooks/templates accordingly.
comms_plan:
Internal
- #eng-releases: publish pilot schedule, patch milestones, gating status, and explicit sign-off requests.
- Support/CS: weekly 15-min sync during pilot; share known-issues link and the backport intake template.

External (per-customer)
- Dedicated: email to customer channel with (a) target maintenance window, (b) expected risk, (c) rollback conditions, (d) release notes link.
- Private: send upgrade package + verification steps (checksums/provenance) and a rollback procedure; confirm the on-call contact for the window.

Patch availability messaging
- For each patch: “What changed (high level)”, “Who should take it”, “Known issues/workarounds”, “How to verify artifact integrity”, “Support contact + escalation path”.
risks:
- Perf gates may be noisy under shared runner contention, causing pilot delays. Mitigation: reserve runner capacity; enforce rerun + waiver policy.
- Backports could create correctness risk if diffs are not minimal. Mitigation: strict eligibility rubric and targeted regression tests (scheduler + KV cache).
- Private packaging friction (pinning, registry access, checksum verification) could consume most of pilot time. Mitigation: do a dry-run with internal Private env before customer window.
- Customer expectation mismatch on LTS (e.g., “all fixes” vs “security/critical only”). Mitigation: explicit comms and sign-off on policy summary before first patch rollout.
updates: 2025-03-06 (Talia Benson): Drafted pilot outline; proposed Northstar Bank (Dedicated) + Helio Health (Private). Waiting on CS/AEs to confirm customer willingness + maintenance windows.

2025-03-11 (Connor O'Brien): Internal kickoff complete with Runtime + SRE + Support. Action items: confirm perf-canary capacity for patch week (INT-3368) and finalize customer-facing cadence language (PM-913).
2025-03-14 (Rachel Kim): Northstar Bank verbally confirmed pilot participation; they want a 2-week heads-up before any maintenance window and a written rollback decision tree.
2025-03-18 (Liam O'Rourke): Helio Health agreed to Private pilot contingent on checksum/provenance docs and a rollback drill. They requested SBOM availability timeline for their compliance packet.

2025-03-21 (Sahana Iyer): CI path for release branch artifacts now produces checksums/provenance metadata in staging. Need to validate customer-facing instructions (docs PR) and confirm signing key access model is acceptable (least privilege).

2025-03-25 (Marcus Reed): Perf baseline for runtime-1.18-lts completed; gating thresholds proposed for p95 latency and throughput variance. Noted one flaky workload on H100 runners; rerun policy required.
2025-03-28 (Connor O'Brien): Targeting 1.18.1-lts RC on 2025-04-03 pending perf-canary runner availability. Dedicated rollout window proposal sent to Northstar for 2025-04-09.

2025-04-02 (Dev Patel): Support intake template for LTS backport requests finalized; will route as SUP tickets with required diagnostics + severity mapping. Need to confirm who approves Sev2 backports when primary approver is OOO.
comments: Connor O’Brien: Please keep pilot crisp: one Dedicated, one Private, and at least one real backport cycle. If we don’t get a real Sev1/Sev2 during pilot, we should still run a tabletop “backport request” using a low-risk fix to validate the automation + approvals + release notes updates.

Sean Gallagher: For Dedicated, we need explicit monitoring cutover checklist: dashboard links, alert thresholds, and rollback trigger conditions. Suggest we define “mandatory patch” criteria now, even if we don’t use it during pilot.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel autotune defaults must remain frozen on LTS during pilot; please ensure customers don’t override flags during perf validation or we’ll get noisy comparisons. We should include “effective runtime config dump” as part of the validation checklist.
Sofia Ivanova: Scheduler smoke tests should be mandatory gate on the release branch before we put any customer traffic on it. Pilot is where we’ll find the blind spots, but let’s not skip the basics.
Rachel Kim: Northstar will ask for change-control artifacts (release notes, known issues, compatibility matrix). We should send them the template early so they can review format before the window.
Liam O’Rourke: Helio needs a straightforward artifact verification story. If the process is more than a couple of commands, it will become a blocker in their security review.
